purpose: Vardenafil is used to treat erectile dysfunction (ED) in men, which means it helps you get and keep an erection firm enough for sex. It does not cure ED, but it works when you need it. It is only for use in adult men and is taken before sexual activity.
how_it_works: When you are sexually aroused, your body releases chemicals that relax the blood vessels in the penis, allowing blood to flow in and cause an erection. Vardenafil helps those blood vessels stay relaxed and open longer by blocking an enzyme called PDE5 that would normally tighten them back up. The result is better blood flow to the penis, making it easier to get and maintain an erection — but only when you are actually sexually stimulated.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, flushing (feeling warm or red in the face), stuffy or runny nose, upset stomach, and dizziness. Some people may notice mild back pain or changes in vision such as seeing a bluish tint or blurry vision. These effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Never take vardenafil if you use nitrate medicines (like nitroglycerin for chest pain) — this combination can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure. Tell your doctor about all your medicines, especially alpha-blockers used for blood pressure or prostate problems. Seek emergency help immediately if you have an erection lasting more than 4 hours, sudden vision loss, or sudden hearing loss. Use caution if you have heart disease, low blood pressure, or liver problems. Alcohol can increase dizziness and lower blood pressure when combined with this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 10 mg taken by mouth about 30 to 60 minutes before sexual activity. Your doctor may adjust the dose to 5 mg or 20 mg depending on how it works for you. Take it no more than once per day. The dissolving tablet (Staxyn) is placed under the tongue and should not be swapped with the regular tablet without your doctor's guidance, as the doses are not interchangeable.
